questionText: Suppose that in an IP-over-Ethernet network, a machine X wishes to find the MAC address of another machine Y in its subnet. Which one of the following techniques can be used for this?
options: X sends an ARP request packet to the local gateway’s IP address which then finds the MAC address of Y and sends to X
X sends an ARP request packet to the local gateway’s MAC address which then finds the MAC address of Y and sends to X
X sends an ARP request packet with broadcast MAC address in its local subnet
X sends an ARP request packet with broadcast IP address in its local subnet
explanation:
Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) is used to resolve a known IP address to an unknown physical (MAC) address within the same local network subnet.

Step-by-step process:
1. When machine $X$ needs to send data to machine $Y$ in the same subnet but lacks $Y$'s MAC address, it prepares an ARP request packet.
2. Because $X$ does not know which physical host corresponds to $Y$'s IP address, it encapsulates the ARP request into a link-layer frame addressed to the broadcast MAC address (FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF).
3. All hosts in the local subnet receive and inspect this broadcast frame. Machine $Y$ recognizes its IP address in the request and replies back to $X$ via a unicast ARP reply containing its MAC address.

Therefore, machine $X$ sends an ARP request packet with the broadcast MAC address in its local subnet.
